rv.q: Kelley's admiring and promising new biographical play...spends most of its 90 minutes looking at Carmichael's childhood...the piece needs a sharper authorial point of view.
The work is expressive, and occasionally moving, but also unvarying in tone.
The performances, direction, and design elements coalesce to create a compelling and thought-provoking tribute to a man whose revolution, indeed, remains unfinished.
'The Unfinished Revolution' serves as a timely and exciting introduction this civil rights activist.
Still, it needs more scenes to showcase the main character's magnetic persona and influential speeches.
Those who are well-versed in the history of Carmichael/Ture may find their knowledge detrimental to enjoying the show.

This compelling production, penned by the talented Nambi E. Kelly and skillfully directed by Tasia A. Jones , was the proud recipient of the Prince Prize for Commissioning Original Work in 2018, a testament to its exceptional quality.
Despite his wonderful acting and that of a delightful supporting cast, a choppy and often confusing story does not live up to expectations.
